summary.headline: Household profile and demographics: published values for FY2020 and how they moved.

statements.text: In FY2020, First-Class and Marketing Mail ads received per household was 487.7 (pieces per household per year). That fell by 155.9 (24.2%) from five years earlier, FY2015.

In FY2020, Advertising mail received per household was 478.4 (pieces per household per year). That fell by 88.4 (15.6%) from the previous year, FY2019. That fell by 150.8 (24.0%) from five years earlier, FY2015.

In FY2020, Correspondence mail received per household was 104.0 (pieces per household per year). That fell by 5.2 (4.8%) from the previous year, FY2019. That rose by 5.2 (5.3%) from five years earlier, FY2015.

In FY2020, Transactions mail received per household was 130.0 (pieces per household per year). That fell by 5.2 (3.8%) from the previous year, FY2019. That fell by 52.0 (28.6%) from five years earlier, FY2015.

summary.headline: Household profile and demographics: long-term change in the published values, FY2003 to FY2025.

statements.text: First-Class and Marketing Mail ads received per household (pieces per household per year) went from 643.6 in FY2015 to 378.0 in FY2025: it fell by 265.6 (41.3%) over the period. Since FY2020 (five years earlier) it fell by 109.7 (22.5%).

Advertising mail received per household (pieces per household per year) went from 899.6 in FY2005 to 436.8 in FY2023: it fell by 462.8 (51.4%) over the period. Since FY2018 (five years earlier) it fell by 156.0 (26.3%). Since FY2013 (ten years earlier) it fell by 213.2 (32.8%).

Correspondence mail received per household (pieces per household per year) went from 130.0 in FY2003 to 98.8 in FY2023: it fell by 31.2 (24.0%) over the period. Since FY2018 (five years earlier) it fell by 15.6 (13.6%). Since FY2013 (ten years earlier) it rose by 15.6 (18.7%).

Transactions mail received per household (pieces per household per year) went from 275.6 in FY2003 to 114.4 in FY2023: it fell by 161.2 (58.5%) over the period. Since FY2018 (five years earlier) it fell by 31.2 (21.4%). Since FY2013 (ten years earlier) it fell by 104.0 (47.6%).
